_note: Which account a platform session is signed in as (src/browser/identity.ts, ACCT-C05). page is opened first; fetch is a same-origin account endpoint read with the session's cookies; emailField is a dot path into its JSON. A platform without page/fetch/emailField has no reader: every run on it is refused until a reader is added and checked live. liveVerified says whether the reader has been seen working against the real site.

claude.note: Same endpoint and field cc browser signin already uses to confirm the signed-in email (data/selectors/claude.json signIn.accountUrl / accountEmailField).

chatgpt.note: ChatGPT's session endpoint; not yet seen live by cc. If it yields no email every chatgpt run is refused (fail-closed), never allowed.

grok.note: Seen live 2026-11-11 signed in (owner-approved read-only GET, t121): HTTP 200, status "authenticated", session.email present, session.signInMethod present as a number (1, an email login; the reader mapped it to email). liveVerified covers status, session.email and the numeric session.signInMethod only; the enum-name form has not been seen live. ACCT-C10. grok.com's web app reads its session from same-origin GET /api/auth/session (its auth client: fetch(`${baseUrl ?? '/api/auth'}/session`)); seen live signed out: HTTP 200 {"status":"unauthenticated"}. Signed in, third-party clients read session.email and session.userId; the login method is prod_auth.Session.sign_in_method (enum SignInMethod, from grok.com's own bundled proto descriptor; the web app's user object carries it as signInMethod). The signed-in shape, and whether signInMethod appears in this response as a name or a number, is NOT yet seen live: no email means unknown (refused); no login method means the provider is unknown, refused whenever the account specifies one.
